P7806.note: The pipeline serves a new fuel-cell facility in central Ohio that will give behind-the-meter power to a data center. The Chesapeake Utilities announcement of July 2025 does not name the campus or the customer. The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects workbook of August 2026 describes it as an American Electric Power Ohio data center campus with Amazon Web Services and Cologix as anchor customers. American Electric Power said in June 2025 that the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio approved onsite Bloom Energy solid oxide fuel cells at data centers run by Amazon Web Services and Cologix, which are two customers at what appear to be two sites. A report from the Columbus public radio station WOSU in May 2025 says the Amazon Web Services contract runs six years and the Cologix contract runs 15 years, that the utility would buy gas on the market, and that capacity and site locations were not disclosed. A Data Center Dynamics article from August 2025 says the pipeline is likely to serve a Bloom Energy fuel-cell facility but calls that unconfirmed. The pipeline is due in service in the first half of 2027 and the data center power starts then.

P8096.note: No single data center campus is named for the main line of this pipeline. A North Dakota Monitor article from August 2025 says the pipeline owner told the state that many interested customers are developing power generation to support data centers. A Grand Forks Herald article from August 2025 says company documents show the line could serve 7,000 to 8,000 MW of data center demand. The same article says an 80-mile extension would reach Ellendale in southeastern North Dakota. Ellendale is the home of the Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1 campus, which Applied Digital said in 2025 is fully contracted to CoreWeave for 400 MW with the first 100 MW building at full load. The Herald says Applied Digital is seeking to grow its footprint and energy demand there. Customer agreements are expected in 2026, and the Pipeline and Gas Journal says construction is slated to begin in 2028.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The data center is a Meta campus in the New Albany International Business Park in Licking County, Ohio. No campus name is given in the sources read. Williams, through its subsidiaries Will-Power OH and Will-Power Pipeline OH, is building two gas-fired power plants called Socrates North and Socrates South, with 200 MW each and 400 MW combined. The Ohio Power Siting Board approved Socrates South in June 2025, and a Pipeline and Gas Journal article from June 2025 says Meta affiliate Sidecat will use the power at an adjacent data center, behind the meter and not tied to the grid. Williams says the target in service is the third quarter of 2026 for Socrates South and the fourth quarter of 2026 for Socrates North. This pipeline would link the two plants, and the same article says the plants' gas will come from two 24-inch pipelines.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The campus is Project Phoenix, a 2 GW data center campus by Aligned Data Centers in the Shippingport Industrial Park, Beaver County, Pennsylvania. It has three planned buildings of nearly 2 million square feet and about $10 billion of investment. Aligned broke ground on September 10, 2026, after the borough approved its conditional-use application in March 2026. The land is about 651 acres next to the former Bruce Mansfield coal plant and is owned by Frontier Group. Aligned says it will use its own onsite power from natural-gas fuel cells instead of the grid, and the fuel-cell supplier and total MW are not public. National Fuel says the lateral gives 205,000 dekatherms per day for a behind-the-meter data center, and that the developer contracted for all of the lateral under a long-term agreement. A Data Center Frontier article from September 2026 says the lateral entered construction in March 2026 and is due in service in late 2026. Frontier Group separately plans a 2,550 MW gas power plant on the same site, which is a different project.

batches/united-states-gas/staging/discov.note: The data center is the Oracle and OpenAI Stargate campus at Abilene, Texas, about 1,100 acres and targeting about 1.2 GW at full build. Crusoe develops and operates it, Oracle leases it, and OpenAI is the end customer. Cleanview says the first 200 MW phase was energized in September 2025 and that the campus connects to the Texas grid and also has about 360 MW of onsite gas turbines. Energy Transfer says it signed long-term deals with Oracle to supply about 900 million cubic feet per day of gas to three data centers, two of them in Texas, and the Energy Information Administration pipeline projects workbook of August 2026 ties up to 900 million cubic feet per day to these three Abilene laterals. These two figures are not the same scope, so the 900 should not be read as Abilene alone. The workbook says the first lateral entered service June 13, 2026 and two more were targeted for mid-2026. Energy Transfer's second quarter 2026 release says a further 14-mile lateral was completed.
